decisions.quote: Recently, we found hypomethylation of OXT in patients with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) compared to healthy controls (HC). Since the replicability of findings is a key point of criticism in (epi‑)genetic research, we aimed to confirm our previous findings in a pre-registered study (data was stored in a database prior to pre-registration) within a new sample of n = 85 patients with MDD and n = 85 HC.
decisions.reason: The current source supplies only the 2024 abstract (n = 85 MDD, n = 85 HC) and the Crossref reference list (bib0001-bib0058), without the article body or in-text citations. The abstract retests 'our previous findings' of OXT hypomethylation in MDD versus HC. In the bibliography, bib0043 (Sanwald et al., 2021, 10.1186/s12888-021-03166-6) examines SLC6A4 rather than OXT, leaving two 2020 OXT methylation papers by the same core team: bib0042 (Sanwald et al., 2020, J. Affect. Disord., 10.1016/j.jad.2020.07.068, shipped row 821) and bib0041 (Sanwald et al., 2020, J. Mol. Neurosci., 10.1007/s12031-019-01446-1). Verified primary abstracts show that 10.1016/j.jad.2020.07.068 (abstract_03) reports 90 MDD inpatients and 90 matched HCs with lower OXT promoter methylation in MDD (p < .01), whereas 10.1007/s12031-019-01446-1 (abstract_04) describes N = 146 MDD inpatients and tests stressful life events, severity, and sex differences without mentioning an HC group in the abstract. However, because the full texts of both 2020 papers and the 2024 body remain inaccessible, one cannot infer from abstract_04 or its title alone that the J. Mol. Neurosci. body lacks any secondary control comparison, nor verify whether the 2024 body cites bib0042 alone or alongside bib0041. Prior adjudication and state files (ae142faf...json, 5c94b3ef...json) do not exist.

corrected_value.title: Academic and Behavior Combined Support: Evaluation of an integrated supplemental intervention for early elementary students

decisions.quote: The purpose of this research was to conduct a practice-based replication of Academic and Behavior Combined Support (ABC Support), a previously developed and experimentally evaluated supplemental intervention that merges a combined focus on reading fluency and academic engagement.
decisions.reason: The 2024 abstract reports a 4-student, 6-week Grade 2 multiple-baseline practice-based replication of ABC Support on reading fluency (trained and standard passages) and classroom behavior (engaged and disruptive behavior), finding improvements 'In concert with prior empirical findings on ABC Support.' Although the 2024 body and in-text citations are unavailable, the complete deposited reference list (bb0005-bb0245) contains only two ABC Support works: bb0085 (Gettinger, Kratochwill, Eubanks, Foy, & Levin, 2021, J. Sch. Psychol., 10.1016/j.jsp.2021.09.004, shipped row 1563) and bb0090 (Gettinger, Kratochwill, Eubanks, Foy, & Schienebeck, 2022, Intervention in School and Clinic, 10.1177/10534512211047571). Inspection of both complete original primary texts resolves the prior ambiguity without claiming same-dataset equivalence: 09_gettinger_evaluation.unrepaired.txt (10.1016/j.jsp.2021.09.004) is the unique empirical evaluation of ABC Support, testing six Grade 2 teacher-student dyads in a randomized multiple-baseline design and reporting significant gains in standard-passage WCPM (59.3 to 72.0, p = .006), training-passage WCPM (60.0 to 91.2, p = .001), classroom engagement (63% to 82%, p = .001), and reduced disruption (18% to 7%, p = .001). Conversely, 10_gettinger_development.unrepaired.txt (10.1177/10534512211047571) is substantive practitioner implementation guidance (10 elements and 15 procedural steps) with no empirical participant sample, study design, or outcome analysis. Under the codebook rule distinguishing reused procedural guidance from the paper reporting the retested empirical findings, row 1563 uniquely represents target_index 0. Prior adjudication da14a543...json exists; prior state f01a2170...json does not.

decisions.quote: A previous study with Virtual Reality (VR) and online motion-capture quantified this approach bias towards food and non-food cues in a controlled VR environment with hand movements. The aim of this study was to test the specificity of a manual approach bias for high-calorie food in grasp movements compared to low-calorie food and neutral objects of different complexity, namely, simple balls and geometrically more complex office tools.
decisions.reason: The 2024 source supplies only the abstract (N = 27 healthy participants performing VR grasp/collection and push/warding movements with high-calorie food, low-calorie food, balls, and office tools) and deposited reference list (bib1-bib73), without the full text or in-text citations. Complete primary texts were inspected for the two candidate VR hand-movement food-bias studies in the bibliography: (1) bib60, Schroeder, Lohmann, Butz, & Plewnia (2016, 10.1089/cyber.2015.0311, shipped row 1827; complete accepted manuscript in 19_lohmann_thesis.unrepaired.txt Appendix A), which tested 23 recruited/20 analyzed healthy participants in a VR + Leap Motion grasp/ward task with high-calorie food and balls, finding faster movement onset (p = .05), contact (p = .05), and grasp collection for food than balls (t(19) = 3.692, p = .002) while noting object complexity as an open limitation; and (2) bib39, Max, Schroeder, Blechert, Giel, Ehlis, & Plewnia (2021, 10.1007/s00429-021-02232-9; 02_max_fulltext.all_text.unrepaired.txt), an explicit follow-up (33 recruited/30 analyzed) using VR + Leap Motion (with fNIRS) and touchscreen category selection with food, balls, and office tools, finding faster food movement onset (p = .043) and touch (p = .017) but slower VR food collection (p < .001) in explicit contrast to Schroeder et al. (2016). Although the 2024 grasp/ward task and faster collection finding align more closely with Schroeder et al. (2016), task differences alone do not exclude Max et al. (2021) from the retested chain, and without the 2024 body's in-text citations, unique attribution to row 1827 cannot be conclusively established. Prior adjudication 44eadc8d...json exists; prior state f17d6adb...json does not.
